Correct, with the positive check preserved via constantDurationValue, but the wrapper is built inline in two places and there is no Pretty fix or error test.
Includes the Pretty fix and a full positive-duration check via `literalDurationValue`. Div-by-zero is not covered and no error tests were added.
Correct wrapping with the Pretty fix and a preserved positive check; tests are limited to round-trip cases.
Adds an AST field and edits many grammar rules plus the generated-file header. Its tests assert that the negative range `foo[-(5s)]` parses as valid, which entrenches a regression.

Adds a public Wrapped field to NumberLiteral and touches ast, printer and several grammar rules (plus a regenerated header); it works and keeps literal checks but is much more invasive than needed, with imprecise positions.
Includes the Pretty fix, and `unwrapNumberLiteral` keeps the `(0)` and div-by-zero checks for the plain wrapped case but not negated ones. No error tests were added.
Wrap/unwrap helpers preserve the zero checks and Pretty is fixed to match String; tests only cover round-trip.
The most complete fix: wrapping, Pretty unary-plus fix, and preserved positive-duration and div/mod-by-zero errors, each with tests.
Unconditional wrap of non-DurationExpr, constantDuration for the positive/div/mod checks, and the Pretty fix, with error tests added.
A reference-like helper that sets both StartPos and EndPos, with an added AST test for `(5)`. It has no Pretty fix and no validation preservation.
Correct helper with proper open/close positions and a new AST test for `offset (5)`; no Pretty fix and the `(0)` validation is lost.

Routes return through ExecError and matches it in walkTemplate; try swallows returns, a bare return yields nil, and the pipeline-reordering normalization plus fake-func template parsing is convoluted.
Relies on unwrapping ExecError, so try swallows return; the pipeline reordering (moving return to the end) is hacky, formatting is off, and a bare return yields nil.

Relies on errorf wrapping with no executor changes; HasValue semantics are correct, but try swallows returns, define/block returns truncate the outer template, and it edits the generated parse/node.go.
Passes the suite and uses HasValue semantics without touching exec, but `try` swallows return, return in template calls ends the whole page, and it edits the auto-generated parse/node.go.
Clean HasValue implementation with try handling and wrapping, but a return in a define/block is not trapped, so a baseof page gets truncated.
Clean, passes the suite, matches reference partial semantics (HasValue, rendered output on bare return) with try rethrow and argument check; lacks a walkTemplate trap.

Clean sentinel with a HasValue flag (a bare return keeps rendered output), handles try and normalizes multi-arg returns; but a return inside a define/block template is not trapped, so an early return in a baseof `main` block truncates the whole page.
Passes the suite with clean HasValue semantics and try rethrow, but has no walkTemplate trap, so a bare return in a block or template ends the whole page; no argument check.
Well-tested and correct for the main cases (HasValue, trapping, try, wrapping), but changes the Executer interface and the executeWithState signature, which is more intrusive than needed.
Thorough unit and integration tests, HasValue semantics, trap, try rethrow and argument check; it widens the fork's Executer interface, which adds maintenance burden.
HasReturn plus discarded output makes unreached returns yield nil, and there is no template-boundary trapping.
No walkTemplate trap, keeps HasReturn discarding, and command wrapping applies only in partials; includes a useful texttemplate unit test.
Gets HasValue and template trapping right, but does not protect return from try, and its tests enshrine silently dropping `return x | f` pipelines.
HasValue semantics with a walkTemplate trap and argument check, but no try rethrow and the trap also wraps the template call's pipeline evaluation.
Has a nice recoverReturn helper and template trapping, but keeps HasReturn so partials with any return never output (and the docs enshrine this).
Nice recoverReturn helper used in both the trap and top level, plus try rethrow and argument check, but keeps HasReturn discard semantics and a bare return yields nil.
HasReturn plus io.Discard breaks partial early-exit guards; there is no template trapping and no try handling.
No walkTemplate trap and no try rethrow, keeps HasReturn discarding, and drops the 'failed to transform template' error context.
Keeps HasReturn with discarded output, so early-exit guards in partials return nil; a bare return yields nil; no trapping at template/block boundaries.
No walkTemplate trap, keeps HasReturn discard semantics and a bare return yields nil; docs and tests are decent.
Correct HasValue semantics, walkTemplate trapping, try handling and arg normalization, with thorough tests; misses the pipeline-position error and edits the generated exec.go.
Clean sentinel with HasValue, walkTemplate trap, try rethrow, argument check and command wrapping; it still traps valued returns in template calls and lacks the reference's error cases.
Adds odd complexity (a user-visible `_returnNoop` func and a neutralizeReturn AST pass), a bare return yields nil, there is no template-boundary trapping, and it drops the transform error wrapping.
Intercepts in evalFunction like the reference but adds a _returnNoop/neutralizeReturn decorator hack; no walkTemplate trap, bare return yields nil, and transform error context is lost.

Close to the reference: a bare return keeps output via HasValue, returns are trapped in walkTemplate, try is handled and multi-arg returns are wrapped; it swallows valued returns inside templates, adds no pipeline-position check, and hand-edits the generated exec.go.
HasValue semantics, walkTemplate trap, try rethrow and moving return to the templates namespace are all sound; it lacks an argument check and traps valued returns in templates.
Correct HasValue semantics, template/block trapping, try handling and arg grouping; it moves return to the templates namespace and edits exec.go directly.
HasValue semantics, walkTemplate trap, try rethrow and argument check in the templates namespace with good tests; changes the ExecuteWithContextAndKey signature.
Traps returns at template boundaries and handles try, but has no multi-arg wrapping (regresses the existing `return add . 42` usage) and a bare return discards partial output.
Traps in walkTemplate and rethrows in try, but has no command-argument wrapping, so `return add . 42` breaks; a bare return yields nil.
HasReturn discards output for any partial with a return, there is no multi-arg wrapping (regression), and try swallows returns; template-boundary trapping is the only plus.
Drops wrapping of `return add . 42`, which regresses an existing feature; also no try rethrow and no argument check, and keeps HasReturn discarding.
Wraps whole-pipeline returns, but has no template trapping and a bare return yields nil; it rewrote the existing issue-13600 regression test into a different scenario.
Rewrites pipelines starting with return so the 13600 regression test now succeeds, renaming that existing test; no walkTemplate trap and a bare return yields nil.
Solid HasValue semantics with a walkReturnable helper for invoked templates and arg wrapping; does not stop try from swallowing a return, and leaves a dangling `[return][]` docs link.
Matches the reference HasValue semantics and adds a walkTemplate trap, but does not rethrow from try, has no argument check, and changes the ExecuteWithContextAndKey signature.
Simple and clean, but has no template-boundary trapping, a bare return discards output, and tests are minimal.
Simple and clean, but has no walkTemplate trap, a bare return yields nil, there is no argument check, and only one integration test.

Keeps HasReturn and writes to io.Discard, so any partial containing a return (even an unreached early-exit guard or a bare return) yields nil instead of its output; does trap returns in invoked templates, wraps multi-arg returns and handles try, but edits the generated exec.go directly.
Has walkTemplate trap, try rethrow and an argument-count check, but keeps HasReturn output discarding and a bare return yields nil; the CopyPipe-based wrapping is awkward.
Traps template boundaries and wraps args, but a bare return in a partial discards the output rendered so far and try is not handled.
Has walkTemplate trap but no try rethrow; a bare return yields nil and the ExecuteWithContextAndKey signature changes.
Reasonable wrapping via a parse helper with try handled, but no template/block trapping and a bare return discards partial output.

Sentinel and try rethrow are clean and WrapArgsInPipe sits in a proper hugo_node.go, but there is no walkTemplate trap, so a return in a defined template ends the whole page, and a bare return yields nil.
No executor changes (relies on errorf wrapping), so try swallows returns, define/block returns truncate the page, and a bare return yields nil.
Relies on ExecError unwrapping, so try swallows return; no template trap, a bare return yields nil, and no argument check.
Keeps HasReturn and discards output, and does not trap returns in invoked templates; it does wrap whole-pipeline returns.
Traps at executeWithState, rethrows in try and wraps return pipelines, but has no walkTemplate trap and keeps HasReturn nil/discard semantics.
Keeps HasReturn with output discarded, has no multi-arg wrapping (breaks `return add . 42`), and does no template-boundary trapping.
No command-argument wrapping, which regresses `return add . 42`; also no walkTemplate trap and keeps HasReturn discard semantics.
Keeps HasReturn with io.Discard (breaks the partial early-exit guard pattern) and does not handle try; template trapping and wrapping are present.
Traps return in walkTemplate and keeps the `return add . 42` wrapping, but `try` swallows return, a bare return yields nil instead of the rendered output, and the HasReturn output discard is kept.
